prompt: Someone on the platform team ran a deployments import from Settings yesterday and it says it only partly worked. What went wrong?
final_text:
Priya Raman's **Deployments** import ran yesterday (2026-10-16, 14:22 UTC). It handles each row on its own, so most of the file went in: **45 of 48 rows were imported and 3 were refused**. The successful rows came through with no warnings. Each refused row points at something that isn't in Wayd.

## The 3 refused rows

| Import ID | File row | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `dep-031` | 32 | No environment was found named `qa-west` |
| `dep-032` | 33 | No environment was found named `qa-west` |
| `dep-044` | 45 | No version was found with id `0b2d4f6a-8c9e-4f1a-b2c3-d4e5f6a7b8c9` |

**1. `qa-west` doesn't exist (2 rows).** Wayd has only three environments, and they include retired ones: `qa-east` (Testing), `stg-us` (Staging) and `prd-us` (Production). The environment keys skip 1 and 3, so there probably used to be more. One of them may have been `qa-west`, deleted at some point. Either the file used the wrong name (perhaps `qa-east` was meant), or the environment needs to be created again first.

**2. The version id on row 45 doesn't exist.** Looking up that id in Wayd finds nothing, so the version was never recorded or has since been deleted. It could also be a copy-paste error, or an id from a different system. Someone needs to find which version that deployment actually shipped and get its id.

## Fixing it

Deployments have no natural key, so Wayd can't tell when the same deployment has been imported twice. **Don't run the whole file again**, or the 45 rows already imported will be created a second time. Once the environment and version questions are sorted out, there are two ways forward:

- **If the file was right and the data was missing** (they recreate `qa-west` and record the missing version under the same id): retry the refused rows on the existing run. That reattempts only those 3 rows, exactly as they were submitted.
- **If the file was wrong** (wrong environment name or wrong version id): put just those 3 rows, corrected, into a new file. Check it with a preflight before importing it.

The run's row data is kept for 30 days from yesterday, so retrying is possible until about 2026-11-15. I can do either one once Priya or the platform team confirms which fix is right.

prompt: How has Falcon (FALC) been doing on velocity and say/do over its recent sprints? I'm trying to decide how much to commit for next sprint.
final_text:
## Falcon (FALC): last 6 sprints

Falcon sizes in **Story Points**. These figures cover the organization's default window of 6 completed standard sprints, from 2026.18 to 2026.24 (8 Jul to 13 Oct). **Falcon 2026.23 IP** (16–29 Sep) is left out because it's an innovation and planning sprint, which isn't comparable with the others.

| Sprint | Velocity (pts) | Predictability | Say/Do | Items done |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.24 (most recent) | 34 | 95% | 85% | 11 |
| 2026.22 | 27 | 78% | 66% | 9 |
| 2026.21 | 38 | 100% | 92% | 12 |
| 2026.20 | 21 | 65% | 57% | 8 |
| 2026.19 | 31 | 89% | 80% | 10 |
| 2026.18 | 40 | 100% | 94% | 13 |

**Summary (story points):**
- **Velocity:** 31.8 pts on average, ranging from 21 to 40 (std dev 6.5). That spread is about ±20%.
- **Predictability:** 88% on average, ranging from 65% to 100%.
- **Say/Do:** 79% on average, ranging from 57% to 94%.

Counted in work items instead: velocity averages 10.5 items (8 to 13), and say/do averages 77%.

### What this means for next sprint's commitment

- **Falcon usually commits more than it finishes.** Working back from velocity ÷ predictability, they committed about 32–36 pts in the four sprints where predictability was below 100%. That's about the same as or above their average velocity. On average about a fifth of committed points don't get done.
- **Predictability is higher than say/do in every sprint.** That means some of their velocity comes from work added during the sprint, not from what they committed to. If you commit to their full average velocity, say/do will likely stay around 80%.
- **The good and bad sprints alternate** (40 → 31 → 21 → 38 → 27 → 34). Six sprints is too few to call that a pattern, but it fits sprints where they overcommit and fall short, then recover the next sprint. Still, if it holds, the next sprint after the strong 2026.24 would be a lower one.
- **Recommendation: commit about 28–30 pts (roughly 9–10 items).** That's just under the 31.8 average and well above the 21-point low. Committing in that range should push say/do toward 90%+ rather than 79%. If they finish early, they can pull in more work, which helps predictability and doesn't hurt say/do. Committing 35 or more pts would repeat the pattern behind 2026.20 and 2026.22.

Take anything known about next sprint's capacity, like holidays or people out, off that figure. These metrics don't account for availability.

prompt: Is Osprey's backlog in good enough shape to plan the next PI from? Mostly I want to know how many weeks of runway they have.
final_text:
## Runway: Wayd can't measure it yet

Wayd wouldn't give Osprey a runway figure. The check needs at least 10 completed work items in its history window, and Osprey completed **7** between 2026-07-19 and 2026-10-16 (the default 90-day window). "Not Enough History" means the check has no grade at all. It doesn't mean the runway is healthy.

I tried again with a 180-day window to get past this, but the response still came back on the 90-day window (`lookbackDays: 90`). Either the setting was ignored or it's capped, so I couldn't get a runway figure out of Wayd at all.

**A rough figure, my own estimate and not Wayd's:** 7 items in about 13 weeks is roughly 0.5 items a week. At that pace the 18 open items would last around 30+ weeks. That's longer than a PI, and past the 26 weeks where Wayd starts treating a backlog as too long. Treat this as a hunch only: Wayd considers 7 completions too few to estimate from, and the number of items is the wrong measure anyway (see below).

## Is the backlog ready to plan a PI from? Not yet

The backlog holds 18 work items, 6 active and 12 proposed, totalling 39 story points. These are the grades from the default thresholds:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Missing Estimate** | **Unhealthy**: 5 of 18 (28%) |
| Net Flow | At Risk: 1.29 items created per item completed (9 created, 7 completed) |
| Stale | At Risk: 3 of 18 (17%) |
| No Parent | At Risk: 2 of 18 (11%) |
| No Project | Healthy: 1 of 18 |
| WIP Load, Old Proposed, Unassigned Active, Carry-over, Closed Parent | Healthy |
| Aging WIP, Oversized | Not Enough History |
| Rank Inversion | Not Applicable |

**What to fix before planning:**
- **Missing estimates:** MOB-232 (rank 300), MOB-234 (500), MOB-236 (700), MOB-239 (1000), MOB-242 (1300). Two of these are already in progress, so the 39-point total understates the backlog.
- **Stale since 2026-06-30:** MOB-237 (800), MOB-241 (1200), MOB-244 (1500). Check whether these are still wanted.
- **No parent:** MOB-234 and MOB-244. Every other item sits under MOB-150, "Offline-first mobile app".
- **No project:** MOB-241, which is also stale.

**One more risk the grades don't show:** all 6 active items (MOB-230 to MOB-235) are assigned to **Marcus Hale**. WIP Load scores as Healthy because it averages 1.0 per member across all 6 members, but the work in progress all depends on one person.

**My take:** there are probably enough items to fill a PI. The problems are that the size isn't known (28% have no estimate), more work is coming in than going out, and there isn't enough completed history to forecast from. Get the five items estimated and sort out the three stale ones before planning. For capacity, plan from the team's sprint velocity rather than a runway number. I can pull Osprey's sprint metrics if that would help.

prompt: Where did the Raptors put their effort between July 1 and September 30, 2026? Break it down by project.
final_text:
## Where the Raptors put their effort, July 1 – September 30, 2026

**The Raptors finished 412 work items in the quarter, and about a third of them (32.7%) weren't linked to any project.** That's the biggest single slice of their effort, and it can't be seen from the portfolio.

Raptors is a team of teams made up of Falcon, Osprey and Kestrel, so I used the **Team Effort** measure. It weighs each team's work in that team's own sizing method and then combines the teams by their share of completed items, rather than adding up story points across teams that estimate differently.

| Project | Share of effort | Items | Team that did the most |
|---|---|---|---|
| **No project** | **32.7%** | 135 | Kestrel (82 items) |
| Mobile Experience Refresh (MOBX) | 26.4% | 109 | Osprey (87 items) |
| Payments Reconciliation (PAYRC) | 18.9% | 78 | Kestrel (62 items) |
| Self-Service Onboarding (ONBRD) | 15.2% | 63 | Falcon (50 items) |
| Billing Export Retirement (BILLX) | 6.8% | 28 | Falcon (22 items) |

All four projects sit in the **Digital Commerce** portfolio, and none of them belongs to a program.

### What stands out
- **Too much work has no project.** About a third of the effort has no link to a project, either on the item itself or on its parents. That's above the 20–30% range where it starts to matter. **Kestrel accounts for most of it: 82 of its 141 items (about 58%)** had no project. Kestrel's backlog is the place to look first. The work may belong to a project and just not be linked, or it may be unplanned work like support or maintenance.
- **Each team mostly owns one project.** Osprey is the main team on Mobile Experience Refresh, Kestrel on Payments Reconciliation, and Falcon on Onboarding and Billing Export Retirement.
- **The three teams were close in size:** Falcon 141 items (34.2%), Kestrel 141 (34.2%), Osprey 130 (31.6%).

### Caveats
- **Some estimates are missing.** 271 of the 412 items came from teams that size in story points, and 23 of those had no estimate. Unestimated items were left out of the Team Effort figures, so the shares lean slightly toward work that was estimated. Re-running with the team average filled in for missing estimates would close that gap.
- **What counts:** only story-level items (user stories, bugs) whose status became Done between July 1 and September 30 (UTC). Epics and features aren't included.
- **No full team-by-project grid:** the report only names the biggest team on each project. It doesn't give every team's share of every project. I can run the report for each team separately if you want that.
